### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **68** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**76** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- **29** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fac58fcdf2db80ae23e2b98b6006d771eea6d948` — the merge of head `35b01a068ea3e350eac34f6e3b8446836550405d` into base `a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fac58fcdf2db80ae23e2b98b6006d771eea6d948 && git checkout fac58fcdf2db80ae23e2b98b6006d771eea6d948
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216 35b01a068ea3e350eac34f6e3b8446836550405d && git checkout -B drift-repro a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216 && git merge --no-ff 35b01a068ea3e350eac34f6e3b8446836550405d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a35fc6656636772766917e79c4d4692d0b7fe216` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#8345#1 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZWjnSeed8H4dMjt9d

Served-tier: TIER_DEFAULT (the seat's own review of record for the `Clause-②: yes` declaration; reviewer: opus subagent of the epic PM seat). Verdict at 90fabf31: **FAIL** (REWORK). The claim's `Clause-②:` line is revised to `yes (widening)` (comment 6640794926, edited). P1 is the seat's own miss: the dispatch order carried no `Writes:` line; this PR will be re-opened through the relay `pr_create`.

Seat review · PR #30181 @ 90fabf31 · TIER_DEFAULT
Verdict: FAIL

Scope: card #27193 (os migrate recompute-home-amounts, M2-3, epic #8345). Diff `origin/main...90fabf31`: 19 files, +1789/-5, no governed surface. Read: card body and comments (scope addition 6498215930, claim 6640794926, os-dev-report 6642646281), PR body, dispatch order `/mnt/project-files/epic-8345/dispatch-27193.md`, execution-duties 复核 + review-checklist.md, ADR-0144 on main (D5, D7 p1, D8 r4, Open items 2/3/6/8/13).

The design is sound. There is one copy of the arithmetic, the work is done per organization, skipped rows are never written, and the Open item 8 proposal is well pinned. The FAIL comes from a required CI job that is red on this head, a docs defect, and one refusal assertion that is missing.

## Must-fix

M1. `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recompute-home-amounts.ts:35-47` (the stamp is at :43). The required CI job "Lint & Repo Gates" is red on head 90fabf31.
- What fails: lane `Lint · docs & code guards` (job 126878559562) fails at gate step "Error-code provenance guard": `@objectstack/cli stamps 'VALIDATION_FAILED' (assign) at packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recompute-home-amounts.ts:43 — not listed under its own owner key`.
- Local check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec tsx scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts` gives exit 1 with the same line.
- Suggested fix, in scope: drop the CLI's own copy of the since check (`refuseMalformedSince` and its second `CALENDAR_DATE`). Instead, export a pure validator from `home-amount-recompute.ts` (`isCalendarDate` + `refusal(VALIDATION_FAILED_CODE, …)`, already stamped in objectql) and call it before the probe. This also removes a duplicate.
- The other fix, a ledger row in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, is behind the dispatch's `packages/spec/src/**` fence.
- Note: the report's "dispatch-gates --commands 105/105 exit 0" is true but did not derive this gate (see P2).

M2. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:1678-1679`: the heading `#### \`os migrate comment-reactions\`` now appears twice in a row.
- The diff inserts one copy at the end of the new section, just above the existing one. The page gets an empty section with a duplicated anchor.
- Fix: delete line 1678.

M3. `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recompute-home-amounts.test.ts:157`: the OBJECT_NOT_FOUND refusal asserts only `code`.
- The envelope carries status 404 (`migrate-object-scope.ts:70`), and the checklist requires `code` + `status` on every refusal case.
- Fix: `toMatchObject({ code: 'OBJECT_NOT_FOUND', httpStatus: 404 })`.
- The other refusals already assert both: objectql (`[code, status]` × 5) and the CLI `--since` / INVALID_FIELD envelopes.

## Process findings (the seat's call, not the dev's code)

P1. `mcp_calls` names a write tool: `github create_pull_request`.
- `.claude/settings.json` deny-lists that tool. Checklist rule: "mcp_calls 点名写工具 ⇒ 拒收,⛔ 不带注放行" (reject; do not pass it with a note).
- Root cause: the dispatch order `dispatch-27193.md` has no `Writes:` line, although execution-duties §派发 requires one ("PR 只经中继 `pr_create`"). On a project thread that line is the only defence.
- The PR itself is draft, base main, with no assignee and no reviewer.
- The seat has to rule on this; the dev cannot fix it in the code.

P2. dispatch-gates under-derived: its 105 commands did not include `check:error-code-provenance`, which CI runs in lint-docs-code. That gap is how M1 shipped with a "105/105" report.

P3. The declaration was corrected from the claim's `Clause-②: no` to `yes (widening)` in the PR body. Per the checklist ("dev 纠正 PM 要当众认", a dev's correction of the PM is acknowledged in public), the seat acknowledges it on #27193.

## Should-fix

S1. More `sys_audit_log` rows than "one per run".
- Under the CLI composition (`buildDataMigrationPlugins({ settings, audit: true })` mounts AuditPlugin), an applied run writes N per-row `sys_audit_log` rows plus the 1 run entry.
- Measured with a temporary probe (removed): engine + `installAuditWriters` + `recomputeHomeAmounts(apply)` over 3 rows → written 3, audit rows 4: `[update a, update b, update c, update null]`.
- The per-row history is arguably right (audit capture is always on). But the docs ("one per run") and the tests only see the run entry, because every test composition lacks the writers.
- Fix: say so in `cli.mdx` / `currency.mdx`, and pin it once with the real writers.
- This is also the first `audit: true` migrate command whose target is a business object, not an excluded ledger table.

S2. Two ways the run is incomplete but nothing signals it.
- `recompute-home-amounts.ts:256`: the CLI exit code ignores `report.truncated`. A `--max-records`-capped walk exits 0 while `homeAmountRecomputeComplete` is false. Precedent `record-currency-codes` does the same, but this command's own completeness rule counts truncation.
- `home-amount-recompute.ts:463`: an unclassified error (for example a rate read failing) is rethrown out of the walk after earlier rows were written, so the run gets no run-level audit entry. Consider try/finally writing a partial-run entry.

S3. `updated_at` is preserved.
- This is safe and has precedent (`audit-key-material`, `comment-parent-pair`; `plugin.ts:1841` keeps a supplied `updated_at` under preserveAudit, and `updated_by` is untouched with no session user).
- Two caveats:
  - A consumer that syncs incrementally by `updated_at` never sees the recomputed home amount.
  - The sibling `record-currency-codes` (#28128) does bump `updated_at`.
- One docs sentence would cover it.

S4. The CLI test docblock (`recompute-home-amounts.test.ts:9`) names `packages/qa/dogfood/test/home-amount-recompute.test.ts`, which does not exist. The file is `home-amount-projection.test.ts`.

S5. The `code_blank` remedy line points at `record-currency-codes --code <ISO>`. Under ADR-0144 Open item 13 / #28128 S1, that command writes one code into every organization's codeless rows. The report already has per-org `code_blank` counts, so a half-sentence warning would prevent a wrong deployment-wide code.

S6. "Writes touch only the home and rate fields" is true of the payload. Engine-side dependents that read the home field still move with it: stored expressions, parent summaries and audit rows (S1). That is the correct consequence of "equals a fresh write", but the docs claim reads narrower.

## Checks (each item of the brief)

1. No second copy of the arithmetic: holds.
   - The preview calls `projectHomeAmounts([entry], row, reads.serving, …)` (`home-amount-recompute.ts:442`) over `ObjectQL.homeAmountReadsFor`, which returns the same private `homeAmountServing` and `homeAmountOrganizationOf` the write uses (`engine-references-and-master-detail.ts:113-118`).
   - The only local numeric code is `sameStoredNumber`, which compares and computes nothing.
   - Apply sends `{id, <homeField>, updated_at}`. `homeAmountsTouched` counts the home field as an input, so the by-id update re-projects over prior+patch (`engine.ts` ~10038-10046). The rate field comes from the write.
   - Fresh-write equality is pinned in memory and on 3 SQL cells. Ablations A2 and A8 in the PR body support the claim.
2. Per organization: holds.
   - The organization is `row.organization_id` under the unscoped system read. `rateOn` runs `{isSystem, tenantId: org}`, so the driver scope is applied per organization.
   - Home currency and counts are per organization.
   - The in-memory two-org pin uses different currencies per org, so it does not exercise rate scoping. The dogfood isolated-posture pin does (EUR rows in both orgs, 0.128 vs 0.9→0.8), and it passes on PG.
   - Writes are by id only. No cross-org leakage found.
3. Writes and isSystem:
   - isSystem skips permission, FLS and the readonly strip. The home and rate values are recomputed anyway (A2).
   - The second validation pass and the D8 r4 code guard still run.
   - Hooks run (see S1).
   - The #27198 lock is on `localization.currency` settings writes, which this run never makes.
   - One run entry per applied run (plus S1).
4. Skip classes: all five are listed, counted per org and reason, and never written.
   - `code_blank` is checked before projection, so it never folds into `rate_missing` (A4).
   - The remedy text names `os migrate record-currency-codes --object …`.
   - The Open item 8 proposal (not written; incomplete with exit 1 on dry run and apply; audit lists skipped rows, capped at 1000) is pinned (objectql + CLI) and is sensible. Rejecting a marker column is right under D8 r2.
5. `--since`: filters on the document date (`rateDate`). A datetime is read in the org timezone via `serving.timezone`; a blank date is outside every window. Pinned at the Shanghai/UTC boundary in memory and on 3 SQL cells (A6).
6. Clause-② yes (widening):
   - Purely additive: new objectql exports, the new `ObjectQL.homeAmountReadsFor`, and a new optional `settings` arm on the CLI util. Nothing narrows.
   - `patch` for objectql and cli is right under AGENTS.md §3 (`Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ patch). Dogfood is private.
   - `homeAmountReadsFor` is necessary given the structural-engine design (`homeAmountServing` is private). It grants no privilege an in-process engine holder lacks. Optionally mark it `@internal`; seat's call.
7. Ledger edits are legitimate.
   - `federated-injected-column-readers` rows: the function does ask `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn` before selecting org/updated_at, and the file passes.
   - `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: re-running `--write` reproduces it byte-identical (`git status` clean). The coverage ledger only grows.
   - The adr-anchors JSON passes `check-adr-anchors`.
8. Tests: refusals assert code+status except M3; exit codes are asserted. The ablations are meaningful (A2 proves the write recomputes; A8 proves the single code path).
9. Scope: no `packages/spec/src`, `skills`, `docs/adr`, `.claude`, `ui` or `apps` paths (grep exit 1 = none).
